extracted.intended_audience: researchers, librarians, institutions, funders, and prospective Faculty Members interested in expert article recommendation services
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and criteria for Faculty Opinions (formerly F1000) expert recommendations: appointed faculty provide short summaries and semantic ratings of research outputs to curate and highlight important literature. The page specifies who may review, what outputs are eligible, transparency/metadata practices, and process attributes (requests, selection, responses).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation content and semantic rating
rubrics_metrics.description: Faculty Members are required to write a short summary of the key interest points in any article they recommend and provide a semantic rating: 'Exceptional', 'Very good', or 'Good'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summaries should highlight why the article is interesting, novel, challenging (and other categories/classifiers of interest). The semantic rating is intended to convey the expert judgement of importance/quality; recommendations are citable via DOI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible reviewers (Faculty Members) and appointment standard
rubrics_metrics.description: All recommendations must be provided by an appointed Faculty Member. Faculty Members are a virtual collection of peer-nominated scientific experts (approx. 8000) and must be Associate Professor (or equivalent) and above.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Faculty Members are peer-nominated and approved by the appointed Heads of each Faculty. F1000 manages the service but does not influence appointments or what is recommended — experts act independently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for inclusion (how an output is entered into Faculty Opinions)
rubrics_metrics.description: A research output (article, preprint, or other type of research output) must be recommended by an appointed Faculty Member to be included in Faculty Opinions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any conflicts of interest associated with recommending a specific output must be openly declared. Inclusion depends on a Faculty Member's recommendation rather than automatic coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible types of outputs
rubrics_metrics.description: Faculty Opinions covers journal accepted manuscripts, other scholarly outputs, and preprints (with scope currently focused on life and medical sciences and expanding to psychology and physical sciences).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The service is broadening beyond life/medical sciences to include additional subject areas; the platform is also working to encourage recommendation of a broader range of research output types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency: open identities and open reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer identity is public; reports are open. All recommendations are assigned a DOI and are fully citable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendations are pushed to the Crossref article record and are citable, increasing visibility and transparency of peer review activity. The service is working to secure ORCID ids for all Faculty Members and to push recommendations to individual ORCID ids to recognize reviewers' efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competing interests / conflict of interest checks
rubrics_metrics.description: Competing interests are checked and any conflicts of interest associated with recommending a specific output must be openly declared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declaration of conflicts is required as part of the recommendation process to ensure transparency of expert judgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Review coverage is of the complete paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Faculty Opinions indicates that recommendations cover the complete paper (i.e., reviewers comment on the whole work rather than partial or fragmentary content).

rubrics_metrics.name: Review request and selection process
rubrics_metrics.description: Review/request dynamics: reviews may be requested by authors; reviewers are selected by editor, service, or community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The review selection model is flexible — reviews can originate from author requests but selection of the reviewer can be by an editor, the service, or the community. The 'Decision' reported is an 'Other scale or rating' (i.e., semantic rating rather than accept/reject).

rubrics_metrics.name: Author response policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are permitted to provide a response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author responses are accepted (Author response = Yes), though the platform currently indicates 'Public interaction = No' for other forms of public commenting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public interaction and commenting functionality
rubrics_metrics.description: Public interaction on the site is currently disabled (No), though user commenting functionality is in development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At the time of the page, public commenting is not available; planned features may allow broader interaction in future releases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript hosting
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscript hosting: No — Faculty Opinions does not host manuscripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The service provides recommendations and metadata (DOIs, Crossref flags) rather than serving as a manuscript repository or host.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and intended use of recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Faculty Opinions intends to provide a route for qualitative (post-publication) review and commenting, complementing quantitative article-based citation metrics with independent expert recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The service is used by research/institution libraries, funding agencies and institutions for research impact assessment, evaluation, and practical services such as peer review selection and grant management. The unique selling point (USP) is recommendations provided by independent experts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope by discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject-scope: primarily life and medical sciences, with planned expansion to psychology and the physical sciences and more to come.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users should expect current coverage to be strongest in life/medical sciences; coverage expansion is ongoing (noted for 2019 on the page).

rubrics_metrics.name: Metadata and discoverability practices
rubrics_metrics.description: All recommendations receive a DOI, are citable, and are pushed to Crossref; efforts are being made to push recommendations to individual ORCID ids.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These practices are designed to improve transparency, recognition of reviewers, and discoverability/integration into bibliographic records.
